root_cause_label: Agent applied a wrong fix (removed constexpr) based on an unverified assumption, then validated only runtime behavior instead of the actual compile-time evaluation requirement
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent removed constexpr without reading the file or the test requirements first, then fabricated a proxy runtime test that passed while the actual benchmark requirement (constexpr for static_assert) remained broken.
t_err_evidence: In step 1, the agent decides to remove constexpr without first reading sum_array.h or the actual test constraints; it assumes removing constexpr is the correct fix without verifying what the benchmark's test_compile actually checks.
t_commit_evidence: In step 2, the agent applies 'sed -i s/constexpr T/T/g sum_array.h', permanently removing constexpr from the header. After this edit, the solution cannot satisfy the static_assert/compile-time requirement regardless of subsequent steps.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed that removing constexpr would make the function C++11 compatible without reading the file first or understanding that the benchmark requires constexpr for compile-time evaluation in static_assert. It also assumed its own local runtime test was a sufficient proxy for the actual test_compile evaluation.
fabrication_evidence: In steps 4-6, the agent creates a runtime test (test_sum_array.cpp) that only verifies sum=15 at runtime, compiles it with g++ -std=c++11, and runs it successfully. This proxy test completely bypasses the actual requirement (compile-time constexpr evaluation for static_assert), yet the agent claims the task is complete based solely on this passing runtime test.
